figures.caption: FIG. 1. Basin of retrieval pattern ξ1,1 according to Eq. (41). Direct-simulation values are retrieval fractions over 16 disorder realizations.
FIG. 2. DMFT endpoint classes. The symmetric class η is identified by equal descendant overlaps near the majority-pattern value (1 + b2)/2.

FIG. 3. Time dependence of the retrieval basin. The same trajectories are classified at both observation times using Eq. (41). Direct-simulation values are retrieval fractions over 16 disorder realizations.
FIG. 4. Readout trajectories at α = 0.05. Dashed curves give (M2 + M3)/2. Direct simulations use 16 disorder realizations per initial overlap.
FIG. 5. Readout trajectories as the loading increases. Dashed curves give (M2 + M3)/2. Direct simulations use 16 disorder realizations per initial overlap.

FIG. 6. Basin selection near the lower retrieval boundary. (a) Direct trajectories from the same initial state with M0 = 0.20, projected onto output overlaps from t = 5. The two loadings differ by one uncondensed block. Diamonds mark the saddles and circles the endpoints at T = 1000. The inset enlarges the saddle neighbourhood. (b) Boundary shifts predicted by Eq. (46) and measured at ten parameter pairs excluded from coefficient estimation. Filled and open markers denote two populations of 106 trajectories. Shifts are relative to each population’s boundary at (0.61, 0.20).

FIG. 7. Self-feedback coefficients and contributions from the two covariance eigenspaces. Horizontal guides select the observation times shown on the right. Color and ordinate scales are set separately for the two conditions.

FIG. 8. Cross-talk noise covariance for t, t′ ≥ 20 and the contributions from the covariance eigenspaces. Horizontal guides select the observation times shown on the right. Color and ordinate scales are set separately for retrieval and failure.

FIG. 9. Integrated self-feedback at α = 0.05 during retrieval and failure. The horizontal line in the retrieval panel is Eq. (48), with U estimated from the late-time resolvent. The inset extends the failed-retrieval trajectory to T = 1000 using 5 × 104 effective trajectories, with the response evaluated by Gaussian integration by parts.
FIG. 10. DMFT input-output pairs at M0 = 1. The solid curves give all roots of Eq. (51) with Λ replaced by Λ(T ); dashed curves give the bare transfer f(y). Points are the finite-time outputs.

FIG. 11. Endpoint overlap under synchronous sign dynamics. Outlines in the upper panels mark the coexistence intervals reported in Ref. [10]. The lower panels enlarge these intervals and the overlap range containing the two mixed states. Values outside this overlap range are shown in grey.

FIG. 12. Trajectories under synchronous sign dynamics. DMFT uses 106 effective trajectories through T = 300; direct simulations use 64 disorder realizations per initial overlap through T = 100. Crosses mark the DMFT endpoints. Insets resolve the two symmetric mixed states, which lie on the dotted diagonal.
